requirements.requirement: Every sudo command run on node1 is logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: sudo's syslog facility was redirected to local2 via /etc/sudoers.d/10-sudo-syslog (validated with visudo -c), and /etc/rsyslog.d/49-sudo.conf routes local2.* to /var/log/sudo-commands.log. Both pre-restart (cmd-de982eebfdc7442e) and post-restart (cmd-d74769a8554842a3) tail outputs show entries with timestamp, user (antrieb), target user, and command, e.g. 'Sep 4 23:56:51 node1 sudo: antrieb : ... USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/id'.

requirements.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log (auth.log/syslog)
requirements.summary: The rsyslog rule uses a 'stop' directive after routing local2.* to the dedicated file, preventing it from also matching the catch-all *.* rule that feeds /var/log/syslog. Evidence from both before and after the restart (cmd-de982eebfdc7442e, cmd-d74769a8554842a3) shows auth.log and syslog tails contain no COMMAND= lines for the same test sudo invocations, only generic PAM session open/close lines (which originate from a separate PAM logging path, not the command log line).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — logging every sudo command with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and excluding those entries from the general system log — are directly demonstrated with before/after tail output on node1, both before and after a full node restart. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is also complete and coherent: pre-restart boot id and healthy state were captured, a shutdown -r now was acknowledged, connectivity was lost then regained with a different boot id, and the sudo logging configuration and behavior were re-verified as functioning identically post-restart. No unnecessary mutations or residue were identified.
limitations: auth.log PAM session open/close lines are still present after the change; these are a separate logging path from PAM (not the sudo command line itself) and their continued presence in auth.log does not indicate command-log leakage, but this distinction relies on interpretation of the log format rather than an explicit executor explanation.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare stage disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation reduces to a single before/after-executor comparison; this is expected given prepare.enabled=false and is not a defect.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (creating /etc/sudoers.d/10-sudo-syslog, creating /etc/rsyslog.d/49-sudo.conf, restarting rsyslog, and the mandated node reboot) map directly to satisfying the task requirement or the independent restart-evidence protocol. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were found. The sudoers.d file was validated with visudo -c before and after creation, and file permissions/ownership were checked (cmd-61cae7c3ec4b49ed) and matched the auth.log convention. The lifecycle diff shows only the expected boot-identity change and transient systemd-private tmp directories from the reboot, no executor residue.
